exposure: third- or fourth-degree tear in the first pregnancy
outcome: third- or fourth-degree tear in a second pregnancy
cohort: Primigravid women with a vaginal birth in Scotland from 1997 until 2010
finding: Women with third- or fourth-degree tears in their first pregnancy do not delay or avoid subsequent childbirth, but they are more likely to have a repeat third- or fourth-degree tear or an elective caesarean section in a subsequent pregnancy.
mod_finding: Women were significantly more likely to have an elective caesarean section in their second pregnancy after an initial third- or fourth-degree tear (n = 887/3333, 26.6%; 12.75 (11.29-14.40)).
